questions.question: Why does the design separate candidate retrieval from pairwise verification?
options: Retrieval cheaply preserves recall over a large index, while verification applies richer evidence and calibrated policy to a small candidate set.
Verification is needed only when the vector database is unavailable.
Retrieval makes exact and perceptual hashes unnecessary in every case.
The separation guarantees all similarity scores have the same meaning across modalities.
questions.explanation: ANN retrieval narrows millions of items to a small high-recall set. A more expensive verifier can then combine features and apply a dataset-specific calibrated decision.

questions.question: At the assumed peak of 60 checks per second and 50 retrieved neighbors per check, how many ANN candidates are produced each second?
questions.explanation: 60 checks/s x 50 candidates/check = 3,000 candidate vectors per second before reranking.

questions.question: A threshold change doubles the review queue beyond reviewer capacity. What is the most defensible response?
options: Auto-merge every flagged pair so the queue disappears.
Keep the threshold because recall always matters more than false merges.
Delete uncertain pairs from the calibration set.
Recalibrate the operating point or narrow the review band while preserving a separately validated auto-merge threshold.
questions.explanation: The operating point must account for error costs and review capacity. Queue pressure must not be hidden by converting uncertainty into irreversible merges.

questions.question: Why store versioned duplicate edges instead of only a final cluster ID?
options: Edges eliminate the need for a vector index.
An edge records the evidence and release that caused a merge, allowing a bad bridge to be removed and the affected component repaired.
A cluster ID cannot be stored in a relational database.
Versioned edges make human feedback unnecessary.
questions.explanation: Clusters are connected components of pair decisions. Edge lineage makes false merges auditable and locally reversible.

questions.question: The embedding service is healthy, but the serving index still contains the previous vector version. What should automatic cluster writes do?
options: Continue merging because both versions contain vectors.
Increase the ANN top-K until scores appear stable.
Freeze automatic merges, return advisory candidates if useful, and restore a version-aligned release manifest.
Retrain immediately on all production feedback.
questions.explanation: Scores from mismatched model, index, and calibration versions are not trustworthy. Advisory detection can degrade safely, but durable cluster mutation must wait for aligned lineage.

questions.question: Which split best prevents duplicate leakage from overstating offline quality?
options: Randomly split individual rows after all augmentations are generated.
Put different paraphrases of one source into training and test.
Split only by text length.
Split by source, time, and duplicate cluster so related variants remain in one partition.
questions.explanation: Keeping related variants and connected duplicates in one partition prevents the model from seeing near-copies of test examples during training.
